disposition_reason: Farm survey in Arauca, Colombia reporting Cd in cacao seeds from 14 farms (mean, SD, min, max; municipality means) and in six artisanal single-farm chocolate bars (68-100% cacao mass, per-bar values by MXRF and ICP), with soil, litter and sediment Cd as context. Primary is a Marker markdown conversion of the PDF (no PDF in library).
disposition_locator: Table 3 (seeds), Results 'In cacao seeds', Table 4 and Results 'In chocolate bars'

study.material_scope: fresh (unfermented) cacao seeds from ripe pods, dried for analysis; artisanal dark chocolate bars made on single farms
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Grown in Arauca Department, Colombia (Arauquita, Fortul, Saravena, Tame); chocolate made by local cooperatives on the same farms from their own beans; not purchased retail
study.collection_period: Dry season (Table 1 caption); year not stated (chocolate IDs carry a '2023_' prefix)
study.sampling_unit: seeds: one composite per farm (4 pods per tree, randomly selected within 1 ha) from 14 farms chosen by ripe-fruit availability; chocolate: 6 bars, each a mix of three units from one batch
study.method: Seeds: nitric-hydrochloric acid digestion, ICP-MS. Chocolate: ICP (Methods say ICP-MS, Table 4 says ICP-OES) and monochromatic XRF (Z-Spec E-max, 200 s reads, duplicate); biological replicates n=3, reading replicates n=2
study.lod_loq: Cd in seeds: LOD 0.005 mg/kg, LOQ 0.043 mg/kg; no LOD/LOQ reported for chocolate
study.basis: Seeds dry matter; chocolate as sold
study.qa: Seeds: 92% Cd recovery with NIST SRM 2384 baking chocolate; method validated in O-ring tests. Chocolate readings compared to NIST SRM 2384 (recovery not reported). Soil CRMs ERM-CC141, WEPAL-ISE-961, recoveries 85-115%

findings.notes: Fresh seeds from ripe pods (not fermented); one composite per farm. No significant difference between municipalities. 14 seed farms selected by ripe-fruit availability out of 180 farms selected around previously identified soil Cd hotspots.

controls.control: Blend beans from different farms/municipalities (north-south soil Cd gradient) to bring single-farm chocolate toward the regional bean average
controls.comparator: single-farm artisanal bars vs regional seed average
controls.outcome: Proposed only; not tested. Single-farm bars 0.586-2.013 mg/kg (4/6 > 0.8) vs seed mean 0.78 mg/kg (n=14)
controls.locator: Abstract; Discussion 'Cd in cacao beans and artisanal chocolate'; Conclusions

controls.control: Site selection: expand cacao into lower-Cd areas away from the Arauca River floodplain
controls.comparator: soil cartographic units and north-south position
controls.outcome: Soil pseudo-total Cd mean 0.48 mg/kg (0.04-2.31, n=180); highest in north near Arauca River; Arauquita soil mean 0.65 mg/kg; overflow-plain unit RVB 0.84 vs 0.42 mg/kg in RVA/VVC/RVD/PVB units (Tukey groups). Seed Cd differences between municipalities not significant (Arauquita 0.9 vs Tame 0.68 mg/kg).
'it is well known that 20% of Cd is lost when the husk is removed' (cited, not measured here)
controls.locator: Discussion 'Cd in cacao beans and artisanal chocolate'

controls.outcome: Mixed literature; cited Bravo et al. 2022 found no significant Cd difference vs fresh or unfermented beans in Colombia, Peru and Trinidad and Tobago

regulatory.product: chocolate with 50-70% cocoa mass (paper writes '0.8 mg kg-1 for samples with 50 ≥ 70% cocoa mass')
regulatory.status: cited as comparator; text also says EU limits range 0.1-0.8 mg/kg by product

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Title and authors differ: primary is 'Assessing the cadmium content of cacao crops in Arauca, Colombia' by Bravo, Quiroga-Mateus, López-Casallas, Torres, Contreras, Mendez Otero, Araujo-Carrillo, González-Orozco; stored lists a different title and authors (Espinosa, Quiroga, Noriega, Castellanos).
Stored says all six chocolates exceeded 0.80 mg/kg ('6/6 exceedance'); Table 4 averages show 4 of 6 above 0.8 (0.586 and 0.715 below).
Stored describes seeds as 'fermented, dried cacao seeds'; primary says fresh seeds from ripe pods ('fresh cacao seeds').
Stored says individual seed values ranged 'from below detection to above 1 mg/kg' and range not tabulated; Table 3 gives min 0.32, max 1.19 mg/kg, SD 0.24.
Stored says chocolate measured by MXRF validated against ICP-MS with MXRF LOD ~0.1 mg/kg; primary gives no MXRF LOD and reports both instruments averaged; ICP column is labelled ICP-OES.
Stored says higher Cd 'closest to the Andean foothills' (Arauquita); primary attributes the north-south gradient to Arauca River floodplain sedimentation in the north.
Stored seed method 'details in supplementary methods'; primary states seed LOD 0.005 and LOQ 0.043 mg/kg and 92% recovery vs NIST SRM 2384 in the main text.
Stored sample_population says 'seed subsamples from 14 farms'; correct, but stored sample_n 20 conflates 14 seeds + 6 chocolates.
unresolved: Collection year not stated in text (dry season only; chocolate IDs prefixed '2023_'); years left null.
Per-farm seed values are not printed (only summary and municipality means); supplementary material not available locally.
ICP instrument for chocolate is inconsistent (ICP-MS in Methods, ICP-OES in Table 4); the 'Cd average' mixes MXRF and ICP and the paper does not state which is reference.
Primary read from Marker markdown conversion; table values could not be checked against the original PDF layout.
Whether 100% cacao-mass bars are unsweetened cocoa liquor/mass rather than chocolate is not stated; classified dark_chocolate as the paper calls them chocolate bars.
